description: Ship Step 9: dev commit blocked by pre-commit hook
remediation: Ship workflow Steps 9/10/Close should commit via a temp branch (`docs/ship-{FID}`) created from dev in a new temp worktree, commit there (branch != dev/main → hook allows), then FF-merge dev from REPO_ROOT. Or: add a hook exception for commit messages matching `[skip ci]`.

description: Build Challenge 2 — 529 Overloaded
Pre-push leakage guard blocked push
Post-merge dev CI red: Payload migrate over Supabase IPv6
remediation: Any GitHub-Actions step that opens a _direct_ socket to Supabase Postgres must use the IPv4 **session** pooler (`aws-1-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`, user `postgres.<ref>`), not the direct host. Transaction pooler (6543) can't run DDL. The Supabase CLI (`db push`) is unaffected — it uses the Management API.

description: Pre-existing `fcte`-forbidden CI gate collides with `source_type='fcte'`
remediation: Plan/design step should grep for pre-existing `forbidden-tokens.test.ts` SCAN_DIR + token policies before introducing a new brand/source-type literal into a scanned dir. Part-1 verify (and any verify touching `packages/services/src/corpus` or `packages/ai`) should run the AI-package `forbidden-tokens.test.ts` gate, not only typecheck + co-located unit tests.

description: Branch push blocked: lint-staged prettier --write disagrees with pre-push prettier --check
remediation: Plan/design/build close + summary steps that push a branch should run `pnpm format:check` (or a `prettier --write` over `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`) BEFORE `git push`, not rely on per-commit lint-staged. Alternatively make lint-staged + format:check share one resolved prettier invocation so `--write` is guaranteed to satisfy `--check`.

description: Build plan-1 spike blocked — opencode not installed
Build WS-7 mirror render — `pnpm bkit install` silently flips opencodeProvider + `--opencode` scopes install
remediation: WS-7 mirror re-render in bkit-repo builds must pin the provider AND select all hosts: `pnpm bkit install --claude --cursor --opencode=<committed bkit.opencodeProvider>`. Better: make install preserve an existing `package.json` `bkit.opencodeProvider` (read-existing-then-default) so a plain dogfood install is idempotent on the provider.

description: bkit-design.md Step 10.4 STRAY guard allowlists only `docs/plans/` + `.bkit/friction.md`, but the design phase legitimately appends sanctioned deferral rows to `docs/deferrals.jsonl` (per rules.md Never-drop) and friction to `.bkit/friction.jsonl`; the squash-merge to dev therefore trips the guard on `docs/deferrals.jsonl`, and the allowlist references a stale `.bkit/friction.md` (wrong extension).

Step 3.1 mcp__github__search_issues returns total_count:0 for every query against cbartens/bkit, including the control probe `repo:cbartens/bkit bkit`. Not a genuine zero-hit result — the GitHub issue-search index is unavailable for this repo under the current token (private repo + fine-grained PAT; same class as the known GH_TOKEN project/admin scope gap). Related-issues context is therefore lost for every design/plan/build run in this repo, silently: the workflow maps 0 hits to `None.`, which reads as `nothing related exists` rather than `search did not work`.
remediation: Durable fix: have the related-issues step run a control probe (a query that MUST match, e.g. `repo:{OWNER_REPO} is:issue`) and, when the probe returns 0, write `Search unavailable.` instead of `None.` — 0-hits and index-unavailable must not collapse to the same artifact text. Consider an `env -u GH_TOKEN` keyring-token fallback (same pattern as the Projects v2 403 workaround) or fall back to mcp__github__list_issues, which is not index-backed.

description: Orchestrator fixed a malformed docs/decisions.jsonl row with `head -n -1 file > new` — a GNU-coreutils-only idiom. On macOS/BSD `head` this errors `illegal line count -- -1` and writes NOTHING, but the shell has already truncated the redirect target, and the subsequent `>> ` append leaves a file containing ONLY the last row. Result: docs/decisions.jsonl went 34 rows -> 1, silently destroying 33 append-only decision records. The `&& echo identical` diff guard gave a FALSE all-clear because both sides of the diff were produced by the same failing `head` (empty == empty). Platform is darwin (stated in the environment), so this is a live hazard for any workflow/agent bash that assumes GNU flags.
remediation: Never use `head -n -1` in bkit workflow/agent bash — use BSD-safe `sed ` (or `awk NR>1` for head-trimming). Two structural lessons: (1) prefer append-only edits over read-modify-rewrite on the *.jsonl ledgers; a rewrite makes total loss one bad flag away. (2) A verification diff MUST NOT be built from the same command being verified — compare against `git show HEAD:path`, which is what actually caught this. Consider a shipped rule under rules.md / testing.md: `ledger rewrites must diff --numstat against HEAD and assert 0 deletions`.

description: Two of eight plan subagents failed their artifact contract in the same session, each needing an orchestrator round-trip to fix. (1) @bkit-plan-complexity-check returned its FULL analysis as chat output and never called Write — `plan-complexity-check.md` did not exist (tool_uses=2: it read the plan and replied). (2) @bkit-plan-update stopped mid-item leaving `Verdict: PENDING` in `plan-v2-reviewed.md`. The workflow prescribes Failure Path for a missing artifact, which is far too heavy when the agent HAS the content and merely did not persist it — and the orchestrator is PROHIBITED from writing the artifact itself (`Inlining subagent steps or producing output directly is NOT compliance`), so the only compliant remedy is a re-invoke.
remediation: Give the missing-artifact case the same in-contract remedy the invalid-verdict case already has (`invoke offending subagent again with ...; if still invalid -> Failure Path`) instead of routing straight to Failure Path — a re-invoke to persist already-computed output is cheap and preserves the subagent-authors-the-artifact invariant. Structural fix worth considering: subagent prompts should state that the FILE is the deliverable and the chat return is only a receipt. Also: the orchestrator should assert artifact existence BEFORE the status/commit call, not in the same `&&` chain — here the premature commit recorded a step-done whose `artifacts` entry did not exist on disk.

description: bkit-design Step 3.1 related-issues search via mcp__github__search_issues returned 0 hits for every query on this PRIVATE repo (control query `repo:cbartens/bkit is:issue is:open` -> 0, while gh api search/issues -> 39). Any consumer with a private repo silently gets `None.` for related issues on every design run.
remediation: Step 3.1 should not accept 0 hits at face value: either run a cheap control probe to distinguish `search broken` from `no hits`, or route through the #341 6b/6c mapped gh fallback. Also widen 6i: `trackers stay on MCP` currently has no guard for MCP returning a silently-wrong empty result.

description: MCP related-issues search returns 0 hits for EVERY query on this PRIVATE repo, in both bkit-design Step 3.1 and bkit-plan Step 3.1 — the step is shared, so the defect is workflow-independent. Confirmed again on #58 (plan) 2026-07-15: probes `counter attempt status.jsonl workflow in:title,body` -> 0, `counter attempt in:title,body` -> 0, `repo:cbartens/bkit counter-bus` -> 0, and CONTROL `repo:cbartens/bkit telemetry` -> 0 despite #234 being a telemetry issue whose body is dense with the word. A 0 from mcp__github__search_issues on a private repo is indistinguishable from a genuine no-hits result, and both workflows' step contracts map 0 hits to writing `None.` — so the artifact asserts there are no related issues when the search never ran.
remediation: Both bkit-design and bkit-plan Step 3.1 must not accept 0 hits at face value: run a cheap control probe (a term certain to match) to distinguish `search broken` from `no hits`, and write `Search unavailable.` on a failed control. Fix belongs in the shared step contract, not per-workflow. Alternative: route through the #341 6b/6c mapped gh fallback once it exists. Also widen 6i — `trackers stay on MCP` has no guard for MCP returning a silently-wrong empty result.

description: Plan subagents fail their artifact contract by stopping before the verdict header, recurring across sessions and across agents. Confirmed again on #58 (plan) 2026-07-15: @bkit-plan-update wrote a COMPLETE 677-line plan-v2-reviewed.md (body finished through its verification section) but left line 1 as `Verdict: PENDING`, and returned a mid-task progress narration (`Now the docs table and Automated Tests, then structural verification`) instead of a receipt. The file is 125KB of finished work gated on one unwritten line. Prior occurrences: @bkit-plan-complexity-check returned its full analysis as chat and never called Write; @bkit-plan-update stopped mid-item leaving Verdict: PENDING. The common shape is the agent treating its chat reply as the deliverable and the file as a side effect, and the verdict header — written FIRST, known LAST — is the field most exposed to it.
remediation: Two structural fixes. (1) Subagent prompts must state that the FILE is the deliverable and the chat return is only a receipt — this session's orchestrator said exactly that in every invoke and the failure still recurred, so prompt wording alone is NOT sufficient; the verdict header being written first but only knowable last is the actual trap. Consider requiring the verdict be APPENDED at the end (or written in a final dedicated step) rather than pre-seeded as PENDING at the top. (2) Step 5.3's re-invoke remedy says `Re-emit ONLY the verdict, do NOT redo work` — that is wrong when the agent stopped with real work outstanding, since a verdict-only re-emit would certify incomplete work. The remedy should distinguish `finished but unlabelled` from `stopped mid-item`. Give the missing-artifact case the same in-contract re-invoke remedy the invalid-verdict case has, instead of routing to Failure Path.

summary: API error mid-subagent leaves a valid-looking artifact that passes every gate
description: @bkit-plan-update was terminated by `API Error: Connection closed mid-response` during plan-apply-scope on #58. The harness surfaced the partial output and flagged it incomplete, but the artifact on disk (plan-v3-checked.md, 736 lines) had ALREADY been written with a VALID `Verdict: CONCERNS` header, zero PENDING markers, and a complete-looking tail — so it satisfied every assertion the workflow step prescribes (exists, non-empty, valid verdict, no PENDING). The agent's cut-off sentence (`Now wiring T5.4 into the gates and verification plan`) was the only signal that work remained. It was real: T5.4 was wired into the matrix, tasks and Gate 2, but NOT into the Verification Plan, which still read `Both new rules demonstrably fire: T5.1 and T5.3` and exercised only T5.3 at Step 4c. A rule that never fires is not evidence, so the gap would have shipped the plan's own residual-risk closure unexercised.
remediation: The verdict header is NOT a completion signal — an agent can write a valid verdict and still be mid-task, so the step gates (exists / non-empty / valid verdict / no PENDING) cannot distinguish finished from interrupted. When a subagent returns a partial-output / API-error marker, the orchestrator must verify the artifact INTERNALLY (cross-check the agent's own claimed counts, and trace every newly-introduced task/symbol through to every section that must reference it) rather than re-reading the header. Cheapest durable fix: subagents emit the verdict as their LAST write AND state claimed counts in the receipt, so orchestrator verification is a diff against a claim rather than an open-ended read. A plan-internal consistency check is mechanical and would have caught this: task count == Done-when count, and every task ID in the matrix appears in both the runbook and the verification plan.

description: CANONICAL ENTRY for this defect; `plan-generate-search-issues-index-empty-private-repo` (ts 1784071225000) was a forked duplicate key for the same bug and is now closed as such. mcp__github__search_issues returns total_count:0 for EVERY query against this PRIVATE repo, in both bkit-design Step 3.1 and bkit-plan Step 3.1 — the step is shared, so the defect is workflow-independent. Three independent observations: design run (ts 1784069979895), a plan run under the forked key (ts 1784071225000, control `repo:cbartens/bkit bkit` -> 0 while `gh api search/issues` -> 39), and #58's plan run (ts 1784094598059, control `repo:cbartens/bkit telemetry` -> 0 despite #234 being a telemetry issue). Both workflows' step contracts map 0 hits to writing `None.`, so the artifact asserts there are no related issues when the search never ran. Disposition is known and the fix is specified (see remediation) but NOT shipped: re-verified 2026-07-16 against dev @ 67e427b6 — bkit-plan.md Step 3.1 still reads `0 hits → None.` and the string `control probe` appears in zero workflows. Hence TRIAGED, not CLOSED.
remediation: Both bkit-design and bkit-plan Step 3.1 must not accept 0 hits at face value: run a cheap control probe (a query that MUST match, e.g. `repo:{OWNER_REPO} is:issue`) and, when the probe returns 0, write `Search unavailable.` instead of `None.` — 0-hits and index-unavailable must not collapse to the same artifact text. The fix belongs in the shared step contract, not per-workflow. Fallbacks worth considering, in order: `mcp__github__list_issues` (not index-backed, so it works where search does not); an `env -u GH_TOKEN` keyring-token retry (same pattern as the Projects v2 403 workaround); or the #341 6b/6c mapped `gh` fallback once that exists. Also widen #341's rule 6i — `trackers stay on MCP` has no guard for MCP returning a silently-wrong EMPTY result, which is this bug's whole shape.

description: DUPLICATE — same defect as `design-step-3-related-issues-search-silently-empty-on-private-repo` (first minted ts 1784069979895), under a forked key. Per .bkit/jsonl.md § Key & References a reworded key forks the entry, which is what happened here: one bug, two keys, folding to contradictory statuses (this one CLOSED, the other OPEN). Closed HERE ONLY to collapse the fork — NOT because the bug is fixed. Two corrections to this key's record: (1) the remediation logged against it (control probe; write `Search unavailable.` not `None.`) was NEVER implemented — re-verified 2026-07-16 against dev @ 67e427b6, where bkit-plan.md Step 3.1 still reads `0 hits → None.` and no workflow contains any control-probe language; (2) its `scope: bkit-repo` understated the blast radius — the canonical entry records `scope: universal`, since any consumer with a private repo silently gets `None.` for related issues on every design and plan run. A later observation (ts 1784094598059) reproduced the bug after this row was closed. Tracking continues under the canonical key, status TRIAGED (still open work).
remediation: Superseded — the live remediation is carried on the canonical key `design-step-3-related-issues-search-silently-empty-on-private-repo`. Do not act on this row; do not re-close the canonical entry without verifying the control probe actually ships in the shared Step 3.1 contract.
summary: Duplicate — consolidated into design-step-3-related-issues-search-silently-empty-on-private-repo; the fix logged here never shipped
Subagent exhausts its turn budget mid-task, leaving the artifact at Verdict: PENDING; SendMessage continuation recovers it without rework
description: Two subagents in one build run stopped mid-sentence with their substantive work done but their artifact never finalised. @bkit-build-plan-execute (sub-plan 1; 104 tool uses / 235k subagent tokens) stopped at 'Let us tick T2.7 and T2.9' — 14 of 20 checkboxes ticked, all files written, log left at 'Verdict: PENDING'. @bkit-build-plan-verify (1-1; 50 tool uses / 129k tokens) stopped at 'Tree restored. Let me record the gaps found and finalise the verdict' — investigation complete and temp edits correctly restored, but build-plan-verify-1-1.md still held only the PENDING template, so every finding was unwritten. Neither was an API error (cf. sibling key subagent-api-error-midtask-leaves-plausible-complete-artifact, ts 1784099048125) — the budget simply ran out. Known precedent outside build: utility-new-release and utility-pre-release-check (maxTurns 50) exhibit the same shape. IMPORTANT CONTRAST with the sibling row: that defect is dangerous because the artifact looks complete and passes every step gate; this one is caught loudly, because the seeded 'Verdict: PENDING' template fails the workflow's no-PENDING gate. The PENDING seed is a defence that works and must not be removed as noise.
remediation: Recovery is SendMessage to the same agentId, which resumes from transcript with context intact — the agent finishes the remainder without redoing completed tasks. Do NOT respawn a fresh subagent: that loses the transcript and re-executes ticked tasks. Orchestrators should treat a subagent return that is a mid-sentence fragment rather than a report as expected-and-recoverable, assert the artifact (non-empty, verdict valid, zero PENDING) as the workflow already prescribes, and continue the agent when the assert fails. Durable fixes worth considering: (a) keep seeding artifacts with 'Verdict: PENDING' so exhaustion fails loudly rather than silently — this is what caught both cases; (b) raise the turn budget for plan-execute-class agents, whose work scales with sub-plan task count (15 tasks here); (c) have sub-plans declare an expected task budget so an orchestrator can size the agent, or split at a task-count threshold rather than the current complexity heuristic.

summary: bkit-build Step 6 routes CONCERNS to Step 7 but Step 7's guard admits FAIL only; no route exists for CONCERNS either way
description: In .bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md the Step 6 (Plan Verify) routing table and the Step 7 (Plan Gaps Remediate) entry guard disagree for verdict CONCERNS. Step 6 sub-step 14 defines a route for PASS ONLY (next sub-plan, or Step 8). Sub-step 15 reads 'If VERIFY_VERDICT = CONCERNS or FAIL — run counter-bus routing ... decide_next VERIFY_ATTEMPT ... step-7 failure-path', routing CONCERNS to Step 7. But Step 7's header reads 'Run only if Step 6 VERIFY_VERDICT = FAIL.' So on CONCERNS the orchestrator is simultaneously told to enter Step 7 and told Step 7 does not apply — and there is no third route, since sub-step 14 covers PASS only. Skipping Step 7 falls through to Step 8 (Plan Verify Holistic), which is wrong on a multi-sub-plan run: Step 8 is the after-ALL-sub-plans holistic check, so a CONCERNS on sub-plan 1 of 3 would skip sub-plans 2 and 3 entirely. Hit live on #58 sub-plan 1 (verdict CONCERNS, failures 1). The parallel construction at Steps 10/11 is consistent and shows the intent: Step 10 routes CONCERNS to Step 11, and Step 11's guard correctly reads 'Run only if Step 10 (CHALLENGE_VERDICT = CONCERNS or FAIL)'. Step 7's guard is therefore a stale narrowing, not a deliberate one. Orchestrator followed the routing table (counter-bus printed step-7, exit 0).
remediation: Widen Step 7's guard in .bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md to 'Run only if Step 6 VERIFY_VERDICT = CONCERNS or FAIL', matching Step 11's wording and sub-step 15's routing. Check the sibling workflows for the same stale-guard shape before shipping: bkit-debug.md and bkit-ship.md carry the same decide_next/remediate pattern. Do NOT instead narrow sub-step 15 to FAIL-only — that would leave CONCERNS with no route at all, since sub-step 14 handles PASS only, and would fall through to the holistic Step 8 mid-sub-plan-loop.

summary: bkit-plan-complexity-check subagent returned full analysis as chat text without calling Write
description: First invocation of @bkit-plan-complexity-check on #341-three-runtimes analysed plan-v3-checked.md correctly (verdict SPLIT, 16-task breakdown) but never wrote plan-complexity-check.md to disk; git status showed no new file. Orchestrator re-invoked once with an explicit instruction to call Write and verify on disk, which succeeded.
remediation: none needed this run (self-corrected on one retry); if recurrent across FIDs, consider hardening the subagent prompt to require a post-write existence check before returning

summary: bkit-design-summary wrote design-summary.md to the main repo checkout instead of the WORKTREE_PATH it was told to cd into, then reported FAIL claiming its required inputs did not exist
description: On 380-roadmap-analysis-refresh, the Context line passed the orchestrator-substituted absolute path cd /Users/christian/Documents/GitHub/bkit/.worktrees/380-roadmap-analysis-refresh per the WORKTREE_PATH pinning fix from #209 (commit 0359884). The subagent nonetheless reported design-v3-organised.md, status.jsonl, and design-*.md as absent and wrote design-summary.md (verdict FAIL, non-empty) to the main checkout at docs/plans/202607/logs/380-roadmap-analysis-refresh/ (untracked) instead of the worktree copy, where all required inputs verifiably existed and were already git-committed. This is the same failure shape as the #209/#216 friction items the WORKTREE_PATH pinning was meant to close, recurring despite the pinned Context line. Root cause likely an internal tool call resolving a relative or stale path before the cd took effect, rather than a missing orchestrator-side fix.
remediation: Orchestrator per protocol does not trust subagent-reported paths and asserts artifacts under the Context-supplied WORKTREE_PATH before accepting a step; on failure to find them there, re-invoke the same subagent with an explicit pwd-verification-before-any-other-tool-call instruction rather than escalating to Failure Path, since the required inputs are provably present on disk. If this recurs across FIDs, consider hardening bkit-design-summary.md so its literal first tool call asserts pwd equals the Context cwd before any Read or Glob.

summary: bkit-plan-scope-check-2 returned full analysis as chat text without calling Write
description: On 380-roadmap-analysis-refresh, @bkit-plan-scope-check-2 (cd into the correct WORKTREE_PATH per Context) returned a complete PASS/Failures:2 analysis with two CRITICAL findings in its final chat response, but plan-scope-check-2.md was never created — confirmed absent from both the worktree and the main checkout via find. Same shape as the ts 1784707678775 plan-complexity-check-text-only-no-write-call row: subagent composes the full artifact content but the Write tool call does not happen (or is dropped) before the final report.
remediation: Orchestrator re-invoked the same agent (SendMessage to its agentId, preserving transcript) with an explicit instruction to call Write and verify the file exists on disk before returning, matching the proven recovery from the sibling key.

detail: Local dev had 4 unpushed commits with slop findings blocking husky pre-push gate. Used clean ship-341-close branch at origin/dev to complete Steps 10-13 and push to dev. Pre-existing commits remain on local dev needing separate reconciliation.
